title: Stalk condition for explicit affine spectrum coefficients
statement: Let $f:X\to S,f\prime:X\prime\to S\prime,g:S\prime\to S,g\prime:X\prime\to X$ form a cartesian square of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Fix a pullback proof for the square of their global-section spectrum maps. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O_X),K\prime\in D(\mathcal O_{X\prime})$ and $\phi:L(g\prime)^*K\to K\prime$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback]. Construct $K_0,K_0\prime,\phi_0$ by [def-pc-affine-spectrum-derived-coordinates]. The stalk condition [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition] for the original data is equivalent to that for these spectrum data. No quasi-coherence, boundedness or flatness is assumed, and no direct-image comparison is asserted.

source.place: lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition, affine spectrum reduction: invariance of equation-bc under canonical spectrum coordinates; Tag 0DJ9 affine-open paragraph

proof.text: Use the canonical affine spectrum isomorphisms and their naturality. They biject points and identify all four local rings and stalk maps, hence the specified tensor-to-stalk map.

For a K-flat representative P of K and coordinates (P,N,t) for phi, tensor pullback along the inverse spectrum isomorphisms is an exact equivalence preserving K-flatness. Its derived counits and canonical composition comparisons identify its derived representatives with K0,K0prime and its induced coefficient map with the explicit phi0. The natural tensor-pullback stalk isomorphism identifies the two stalk complexes and the termwise map.

Exactness of stalks identifies cohomology. The local ring isomorphisms identify the derived tensor models by uniqueness of left-derived scalar extension; both model counit equations identify the comparison maps, so the original and transported stalk comparisons are conjugate by source and target isomorphisms. IsIso is preserved and reflected. Fixed-square coordinate invariance extends this to arbitrary coordinate representatives on each side. Bijectivity on points and inverse transport prove both directions, including empty schemes.

theorem affineSpectrumCoordinates_stalkCondition
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S']
    (sq0 : IsPullback (Spec.map g'.appTop) (Spec.map f'.appTop)
      (Spec.map f.appTop) (Spec.map g.appTop))
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (K' : schemeDerivedCategory X')
    (φ : (derivedPullback g').obj K ⟶ K') :
    SingleComplexBaseChange.StalkCondition f f' g g' sq K K' φ ↔
      SingleComplexBaseChange.StalkCondition
        (Spec.map f.appTop) (Spec.map f'.appTop)
        (Spec.map g.appTop) (Spec.map g'.appTop) sq0
        (affineSpectrumDerivedObject X K) (affineSpectrumDerivedObject X' K')
        (affineSpectrumDerivedMorphism g' K K' φ)
